reason: The cited evidence directly supports all key premises: E1 explicitly states that thermo-mechanical processing of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 creates an ultrafine duplex microstructure with hierarchical heterogeneity, leading to simultaneous strength-ductility improvement via constraint and crack-arresting mechanisms. E2 provides specific quantitative data showing that cold-rolling plus annealing yields 1.2 GPa strength and 12% elongation, and cryo-rolling plus annealing yields 1.47 GPa and 14% elongation, confirming the simultaneous enhancement. The hypothesis accurately represents these findings.
premises: Thermo-mechanical processing can refine the lamellar structure of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 into an ultrafine duplex microstructure.
This refined hierarchical microstructure improves both strength and ductility simultaneously.
The mechanism involves a two-hierarchical constraint effect and a self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanism.
Cold-rolling and annealing of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 can achieve high strength (up to 1.2 GPa) with retained ductility (~12%).
Cryo-rolling and annealing can further increase strength (1.47 GPa) while even increasing ductility (14%).
